comment: What each shipped artifact is allowed to weigh. `scripts/check-size.mjs` reads this, measures what was actually built, and fails a release over the limit - a budget nobody enforces is a wish. Limits carry roughly 10-20% headroom over the measured sizes at 0.3.16, so normal churn passes and a payload that doubles does not. `match` is a regular expression against the file name inside the directories searched; `dir` names a whole directory, measured recursively.

budgets.name: loader APK
budgets.why: the lean half: 276 KB at 0.3.16 (552 KB runtime + 142 KB addons bundle, both deflated). Over 400 KB means the phone client is carrying something it did not ship with.

budgets.name: manager APK
budgets.why: 6.6 MB at 0.3.16, of which the embedded loader and the LSPatch runtime are most. Over 8 MB is a dependency or a resource tree that grew, not a feature.

budgets.name: packed app (app.asar)
budgets.why: 4.9 MB at 0.3.16: 2.5 MB of runtime, 218 KB of its stylesheet, 194 KB of plugin manifest, the src/ tree and prod node_modules. The `files` whitelist already excludes both vendored source trees and every .map file.

budgets.name: unpacked desktop app
budgets.why: 325 MB at 0.3.16 - Chromium, ICU, the ffmpeg build and the helper binaries. Almost all of it is Electron, so a jump here is a dependency that was installed into the app rather than into the build.

budgets.name: desktop installer
budgets.why: the 0.3.5 x64 setup was 98.9 MB with compression: maximum and electronLanguages pinned to en-US. Two of anything like it on one release page is what the budget is for.
